title: Valuation evidence has 90-day relevance
full_text:
SMSF trustees should aim to provide their auditor with comparative sales data and supporting evidence for the valuation of an asset that is no more than 90 days old, with information beyond that timeframe posing risks for practitioners, an SMSF legal specialist has noted.
DBA Lawyers special counsel Bryce Figot said his general rule for what was acceptable from an ATO perspective in relation to the provision of evidence was three months based on interactions his clients have had with the regulator.
“Three months is not a statement you are necessarily going to find in formal ATO documentation, but that’s based on experiences I have had in dealing with them,” Figot stated at the recent Auditors Institute Auditors Day 2026 in Melbourne.
“My interaction with auditors happens when things go wrong, when the ATO audits the auditor, and I can think of a couple of specific matters where they went outside that three-month period and the ATO wrote in position papers that they should have picked something within a three-month period.
“So if you, the auditor, are being asked to accept something that’s outside of that three-month period, push it back onto the client and ask why [you should accept it].
“How much are you charging for your audit and how much risk is the client asking you to wear?
“Look at all the work you have to do for an audit. The ATO has updated their guidance from 10 August around limited recourse borrowing arrangements with the extra work auditors are supposed to do, and everything is accumulating more and more onto the work of auditors.
“It may potentially be laziness [by your client], potentially it’s something else, but if it’s not the closest thing to 30 June, you have to ask why and document your thought process.
“If you want me to cite a public document from the ATO, I couldn’t, but the short answer is three months, or ideally 30 June, otherwise push it back to the client.”
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation and Investments
